items.entity: bottom supports (which part of the base is fixed)
items.description: Nanopillar section: pillar is 'supported at the four corners of the base' and load must reach 'the four corner supports'; but the same paragraph calls the 12,800 passive atoms 'the clamped base' and Methods state passive atoms 'are held fixed in all Cartesian directions'. With a0=4.05 Å, 12,800 = 4×40×40×2, i.e. exactly a full-width 2-unit-cell (8.1 Å) slab, so fixing all passive atoms would clamp the entire bottom face. FEM-TO boundary conditions (Suppl. Note A.14) not provided.
readings: Only four corner regions of the bottom face fixed in x,y,z; rest of bottom face free
Entire 162×162 Å bottom face clamped (all passive base atoms fixed)
Full-width 8.1 Å base slab kept solid but elastic, with only its four corner regions fixed

items.description: 'Four corners of the base' gives no size; point vs. patch support and the patch dimension are not stated (setup presumably only in Suppl. Fig. S17 / Note A.14).
readings: single corner node at each of the four bottom corners
1×1 element patch (≈4.05×4.05 Å, 2.5% of width) per corner
2×2 element patch (≈8.1×8.1 Å, 5% of width) per corner
≈10×10 unit-cell patch (40.5×40.5 Å, 25% of width) per corner, e.g. if the 12,800 passive atoms are four 10×10×8-cell corner blocks

items.entity: passive (always-solid) base region in the FEM model / designable height
items.description: Only the count '12,800 passive atoms from the clamped base' is given; their geometry is not described, and it is not stated whether FEM-TO keeps them as solid non-design elements. The count fits a full 162×162×8.1 Å slab at the bottom of the 413.10 Å box (active height 405 Å = 100 cells; 640,000 = 4×40×40×100), but also other arrangements (e.g. four corner blocks of 800 cells each).
readings: Full-width solid non-design slab 162×162×8.1 Å at the bottom; design region 162×162×405 Å above
Four solid non-design corner blocks totalling 12,800 atoms (e.g. 40.5×40.5×32.4 Å each)
No passive elements; whole 162×162×413.10 Å box designable, supports applied directly to design nodes

items.description: Main text and Methods: vertical displacement 'applied at the center of the top surface' (red arrow in Fig. 6a). The number of loaded atoms/nodes or the patch size is not given. A displacement of 1% of height (~4.1 Å, larger than a0) suggests a group of atoms rather than a single atom.
readings: single node at the top-face centre (x=y=81 Å)
small central patch ≈1–2 unit cells (4.05–8.1 Å square)
moderate central patch ≈10×10 cells (40.5 Å, 25% of width)
patch equal to the initial column top, 18×18 cells (72.9 Å, 45% of width)

items.entity: how the top load is imposed in FEM-TO (force vs prescribed displacement)
items.description: The atomistic runs use a prescribed displacement (Methods). It is not stated whether FEM-TO used a nodal force, a uniform traction, or a prescribed rigid-patch displacement, or whether the loaded nodes are free laterally (Suppl. Note A.14 absent).
readings: nodal point force(s), standard minimum compliance
uniform pressure over the loaded patch
prescribed uniform vertical displacement of loaded nodes (rigid punch), lateral DOFs free
prescribed displacement with lateral DOFs of loaded nodes also fixed

items.description: Methods: δ_pillar = 1% of 'the pillar height'. The height may be the full 413.10 Å box or the 405 Å active part. The FEM-TO load magnitude is not given.
readings: 4.131 Å prescribed displacement (1% of 413.10 Å)
4.05 Å prescribed displacement (1% of 405 Å)
unit force

items.description: Text gives a target mass ratio of 20.25% and says FEM-TO solves 'the same nanopillar problem'. Arithmetic (cantilever 88,500/148,500 = 59.60%; (18/40)^2 = 0.2025) suggests the ratio is counted over active atoms only, but the basis of the FEM volume constraint relative to the base region is not stated.
readings: 0.2025 of the 162×162×405 Å active design region (base excluded)
0.2025 of the full 162×162×413.10 Å box, no passive base
20.25% of the full box including a solid 8.1 Å base slab, i.e. ≈0.187 of the design region

items.description: Only the atomistic material is given (Mishin EAM Al, a0 = 4.05 Å, described as 'nearly isotropic'). Continuum constants for FEM-TO would be in the absent Suppl. Note A.14.
readings: E = 70 GPa (bulk aluminium)
E = 1 (normalized)
E derived from the EAM potential's elastic constants

items.entity: Poisson's ratio / elastic symmetry in FEM-TO
items.description: Not given. The atomistic Al lattice is cubic with cube axes along x,y,z but is described as nearly isotropic; the FEM-TO constitutive choice is unknown.
readings: isotropic ν = 0.33
isotropic ν = 0.30
isotropic ν ≈ 0.35
cubic anisotropic Al aligned with the cube axes

items.description: No element size or count is given for FEM-TO. The domain is 40×40×102 conventional FCC cells (a0 = 4.05 Å), and the result is 'mapped onto the same FCC lattice' (Results, Suppl. Note A.14 absent).
readings: 40×40×102 hexahedra (one per unit cell, 4.05 Å)
40×40×100 design elements for the active part plus a base layer
80×80×204 hexahedra (2.025 Å, one per atomic plane)
coarser 20×20×51 hexahedra (8.1 Å)

items.description: No filter is stated for FEM-TO. The Nano-TO default r_min = 10.325 Å (Methods, Sensitivity filtering) may or may not have been carried over.
